title: What Is a Microcontroller?
summary: Look right at the middle of your Arduino board.

steps.title: What Is a Microcontroller?
steps.markdownContent: The black chip is the microcontroller. It runs your code. The blue board holds the chip and makes it easier to connect to a computer and other parts.

quickCheck.question: Which of these everyday machines has a tiny computer inside it?
options: A microwave oven with a digital timer
quickCheck.explanation: Microwaves use tiny microcontroller computers to count seconds, read button presses, and heat food!
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Many household gadgets that beep, show numbers, or have buttons have tiny computers inside them.

quickCheck.question: Why does a computer chip need memory?
options: To store instructions so it knows what to do
quickCheck.explanation: Memory holds the instructions and numbers a computer needs to do its job!
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Just like you use memory to remember a phone number or story, computers use memory to remember code instructions.

steps.title: Inside the Chip: CPU, Flash, and RAM
steps.markdownContent: Think of Flash as a recipe book for saved code and RAM as a tiny scratchpad for information used while the program runs. The Uno also has memory for saved settings.

steps.title: CPU vs Memory Signal Flow
steps.markdownContent: Follow the path: saved code → processor → pin. Tap each part to see how the program reaches an LED.

nodes.label:
1. FLASH MEMORY
(Permanent Storage)
nodes.role: Stores your uploaded C++ program safely, keeping code ready even when disconnected from power.
nodes.example: 32 KB Flash holding setup() and loop() instructions

nodes.label:
2. CPU PROCESSOR
(The Thinker)
nodes.role: Fetches code instructions at 16 million clock cycles per second and calculates logic decisions.

nodes.label:
3. SRAM SCRATCHPAD
(Active Memory)
nodes.role: Holds temporary numbers and sensor readings while the sketch is actively running.
nodes.example: 2 KB RAM tracking timer counts and light levels

nodes.label:
4. I/O PINS
(Hardware Bridge)
nodes.role: Translates internal CPU bits into physical electrical voltages on the Uno pin headers.
nodes.example: Pin 13 sending 5V to the built-in amber LED

steps.title: Microcontroller Knowledge Checkpoint
steps.markdownContent: Prove your understanding of what makes a microcontroller tick!

interactiveConfig.question: What is the primary difference between a microcontroller and a desktop computer?
options: A microcontroller is built to control physical hardware and live inside devices without a monitor
A microcontroller has a 50-inch display screen built in
A microcontroller can only be used to bake cookies
interactiveConfig.explanation: Microcontrollers are self-contained computer chips specialized for interacting with physical sensors and circuits.
